---
title: Extract time series for polygon
---



```js
// This script extract the Sentinel 2 Band Values for all the scenes in the specified time frame

// --> You get multiple date values for each point

// If you put in a polygon, you get all pixel in the polygon

var samples = ee.FeatureCollection("projects/ee-ludwigm6/assets/luenten/extent");





function maskS2clouds(image) {
  var scl = image.select('SCL');
  var wantedPixels = scl.gt(3).and(scl.lt(7)).or(scl.eq(1)).or(scl.eq(2));
  return image.updateMask(wantedPixels)
}

var collection = ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S2_SR')
    .filterBounds(samples.geometry().bounds())
    .filterDate('2017-05-01', '2017-09-30')
    .map(maskS2clouds)
    .select('B2', 'B3', 'B4', 'B8')


// iterate over all images in the image collection and
// extract the values
var sampledPoints = collection.map(function (image) {
  return image.sampleRegions({
  collection: samples,
  geometries: true,
  scale: 10});
}).flatten();


Export.table.toDrive(sampledPoints);
```




The result is pretty messy. In the `system.index` column, the temporal information is burried in the string.
In the `.geo` column, the coordinates of the points (in case of polygon, all pixel) are stored besides some earth engine specific formating.
Here is a R script for postprocessing.


```r

library(sf)
library(tidyverse)


f = read.csv("~/Downloads/myExportTableTask.csv")

# extract time 
f$date = str_sub(f$system.index, 1, 8) 

# extract coordinates with some regex magic
f$x = str_extract(string = f$.geo, pattern = "(?<=\\[)(.*)(?=,)") |> as.numeric()
f$y = str_extract(string = f$.geo, pattern = "(?<=[0-9],)(.*)(?=\\])") |> as.numeric()


f = st_as_sf(f, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326)
plot(f)







```
